papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.authors: Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., Parmar, N., et al.
papers.abstract: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.authors: Devlin, J., Chang, M. W., Lee, K., & Toutanova, K.
papers.abstract: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

papers.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.authors: Brown, T., Mann, B., Ryder, N., et al. (OpenAI)
papers.abstract: We show that scaling language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even competitive with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches. GPT-3, with 175 billion parameters, achieves strong performance on NLP datasets including translation, question answering, and cloze tasks.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.authors: He, K., Zhang, X., Ren, S., & Sun, J. (Microsoft)
papers.abstract: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence showing that these residual networks are easier to optimize and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.authors: Goodfellow, I., Pouget-Abadie, J., Mirza, M., et al.
papers.abstract: We propose a new framework for estimating generative models via an adversarial process, in which we simultaneously train two models: a generative model G that captures the data distribution, and a discriminative model D that estimates the probability that a sample came from the training data rather than G.

papers.title: Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.authors: Zhang, S., Dong, L., Li, X., et al.
papers.abstract: This paper provides a systematic review of instruction tuning in large language models, discussing datasets, methodologies, and benchmarks for human alignment. We cover approaches from FLAN to InstructGPT, with a comprehensive taxonomy of instruction datasets.

papers.title: Comparison of Quantum Cryptography Protocols in Smart Grids
papers.authors: Siddique, U., Rahman, M., & Islam, R.
papers.abstract: We evaluate BB84, E91, and B92 protocols in power transmission grids under noise constraints, providing real-world key generation rate comparisons and security assessments for critical infrastructure protection.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Smart Grid Load Balancing
papers.authors: Wang, X., Li, Y., & Chen, Z.
papers.abstract: A deep Q-learning approach to dynamic load dispatching in microgrids to minimize peaks, showing an 18% cost reduction compared to legacy heuristic methods. Our approach adapts to real-time demand fluctuations using a continuous action space.

papers.title: AI-Augmented Syllabus Design in Higher Education
papers.authors: Miller, A., Thompson, R., & Garcia, L.
papers.abstract: Evaluating standard and agent-synthesized curricula in undergraduate computer science programs. Results show improved engagement rates with personalized pathways and a 22% improvement in learning outcome assessments.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.authors: Ho, J., Jain, A., & Abbeel, P.
papers.abstract: We present high quality image synthesis results using diffusion probabilistic models, a class of latent variable models inspired by considerations from nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Our best results are obtained by training on a weighted variational bound designed according to a novel connection between diffusion probabilistic models and denoising score matching with Langevin dynamics.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.authors: Dosovitskiy, A., Beyer, L., Kolesnikov, A., et al. (Google Brain)
papers.abstract: While the Transformer architecture has become the de-facto standard for NLP tasks, its applications to computer vision remain limited. In vision, attention is either applied in conjunction with convolutional networks, or used to replace certain components of convolutional networks while keeping their overall structure in place.

papers.title: Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction with AlphaFold
papers.authors: Jumper, J., Evans, R., Pritzel, A., et al. (DeepMind)
papers.abstract: We developed AlphaFold, an AI system that predicts a protein's 3D structure from its amino acid sequence with atomic-level accuracy. This is a major scientific challenge that has resisted progress for 50 years. AlphaFold's prediction results are competitive with results from experimental techniques in many cases.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.authors: Touvron, H., Lavril, T., Izacard, G., et al. (Meta AI)
papers.abstract: We introduce LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters. We train our models on trillions of tokens, and show that it is possible to train state-of-the-art models using publicly available datasets exclusively.

papers.title: Ransomware Detection Using Deep Neural Networks: A Behavioral Analysis
papers.authors: Kara, I., & Aydos, M.
papers.abstract: This study proposes a deep learning-based ransomware detection framework that analyzes API call sequences and file system behaviors. Our model achieves 98.4% accuracy on a balanced dataset of 18,000 malware samples across 22 ransomware families.

papers.title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Classical Perspective
papers.authors: Ciliberto, C., Herbster, M., Ialongo, A. D., et al.
papers.abstract: We critically analyze the potential for quantum speedup in machine learning tasks. We discuss the opportunities and limitations of quantum computing for kernel methods, optimization, and sampling-based algorithms, providing a balanced assessment of near-term and long-term prospects.

papers.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
papers.authors: Brohan, A., Brown, N., Carbajal, J., et al. (Google DeepMind)
papers.abstract: We study how vision-language models trained on Internet-scale data can be incorporated directly into end-to-end robot control to boost generalization and enable emergent semantic reasoning. Our experiments suggest RT-2 demonstrates substantially better generalization and emergent capabilities compared to other baselines.

papers.title: Automated Machine Learning: A Survey of Methods, Systems, and Challenges
papers.authors: He, X., Zhao, K., & Chu, X.
papers.abstract: AutoML aims to automate the design of machine learning pipelines. We survey recent advances in neural architecture search, hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, and data augmentation. We also identify open challenges and future directions for the field.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.authors: Radford, A., Kim, J. W., Hallacy, C., et al. (OpenAI)
papers.abstract: We study the behaviors of a system that learns visual representations from natural language supervision. Using a dataset of 400 million image-text pairs collected from the internet, we train CLIP which learns to predict which caption goes with which image and demonstrates impressive zero-shot transfer capabilities.

papers.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.authors: Krizhevsky, A., Sutskever, I., & Hinton, G. E.
papers.abstract: We trained a large, deep convolutional neural network on the ImageNet dataset and achieved substantially better results than previous methods. Our model won the ILSVRC-2012 competition by a large margin and demonstrated that deep CNNs can dramatically improve large-scale image classification.

papers.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
papers.authors: Redmon, J., Divvala, S., Girshick, R., & Farhadi, A.
papers.abstract: We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work repurposes classifiers for detection; YOLO reframes detection as a single regression problem, predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation.

papers.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.authors: Ronneberger, O., Fischer, P., & Brox, T.
papers.abstract: There is large agreement that successful training of deep networks requires many thousands of annotated training samples. In this paper, we present a network and training strategy that relies on data augmentation to use the available annotated samples more efficiently.

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Rombach, R., Blattmann, A., Lorenz, D., Esser, P., & Ommer, B.
papers.abstract: By decomposing the image formation process into a sequential application of denoising autoencoders, diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art synthesis results. We apply diffusion models in the latent space of powerful pretrained autoencoders, enabling efficient high-resolution image synthesis.

papers.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
papers.authors: Mikolov, T., Chen, K., Corrado, G., & Dean, J.
papers.abstract: We propose two novel model architectures for computing continuous vector representations of words from very large datasets. The quality of these representations is measured in a word similarity task and used as input features for NLP systems.

papers.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
papers.authors: Radford, A., Narasimhan, K., Salimans, T., & Sutskever, I. (OpenAI)
papers.abstract: Natural language understanding comprises a wide range of diverse tasks. We demonstrate that large gains on these tasks can be realized by generative pre-training of a language model on a diverse corpus of unlabeled text, followed by discriminative fine-tuning on each specific task.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Wei, J., Wang, X., Schuurmans, D., et al. (Google Research)
papers.abstract: We explore how generating a chain of thought — a series of intermediate reasoning steps — significantly improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning. Chain-of-thought prompting achieves strong results on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.authors: Lewis, P., Perez, E., Piktus, A., et al. (Facebook AI)
papers.abstract: We combine parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation by pre-training a seq2seq model and retrieving passages from a dense vector index of Wikipedia. RAG models generate more specific, diverse, and factual language than baseline seq2seq models.

papers.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
papers.authors: Chowdhery, A., Narang, S., Devlin, J., et al. (Google Research)
papers.abstract: We introduce PaLM, a 540-billion parameter dense decoder-only transformer trained on 780 billion tokens. PaLM demonstrates continued benefits of scaling and achieves state-of-the-art few-shot learning results on hundreds of language understanding and generation benchmarks.

papers.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
papers.authors: Gu, A., & Dao, T.
papers.abstract: Foundation models, now powering most exciting applications in deep learning, are almost universally based on the Transformer architecture. We propose Mamba, a selective state space model that achieves Transformer-quality performance with linear scaling in sequence length.

papers.title: Human-Level Control Through Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Mnih, V., Kavukcuoglu, K., Silver, D., et al. (DeepMind)
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that a convolutional neural network trained with a variant of Q-learning can learn successful policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs using end-to-end reinforcement learning, achieving human-level performance on 49 Atari 2600 games.

papers.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
papers.authors: Srivastava, N., Hinton, G., Krizhevsky, A., Sutskever, I., & Salakhutdinov, R.
papers.abstract: Deep neural nets with a large number of parameters are very powerful machine learning systems. However, overfitting is a serious problem. Dropout is a technique for addressing this problem by randomly dropping units during training, which prevents units from co-adapting too much.

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.authors: Ioffe, S., & Szegedy, C.
papers.abstract: Training deep neural networks is complicated by internal covariate shift. We propose batch normalization, a technique that normalizes layer inputs for each mini-batch, dramatically reducing the number of training steps required to reach the same accuracy.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
papers.authors: McMahan, B., Moore, E., Ramage, D., Hampson, S., & y Arcas, B. A.
papers.abstract: We consider the federated learning setting where data is distributed across devices and communication is expensive. We propose FederatedAveraging, which trains deep networks on decentralized data with reduced communication rounds while maintaining privacy of local datasets.

papers.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
papers.authors: Gilmer, J., Schoenholz, S. S., Riley, P. F., Vinyals, O., & Dahl, G. E.
papers.abstract: We reformulate existing models as instances of a general framework called message passing neural networks, which directly operate on graphs. MPNNs achieve state-of-the-art results on molecular property prediction and provide a unified view of graph neural networks.

papers.title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
papers.authors: Dean, J., & Ghemawat, S. (Google)
papers.abstract: MapReduce is a programming model and associated implementation for processing and generating large data sets. Users specify a map function that processes a key/value pair and a reduce function that merges all intermediate values associated with the same intermediate key.

papers.title: A Note on Two Problems in Connexion with Graphs
papers.authors: Dijkstra, E. W.
papers.abstract: We consider two problems concerning the shortest path through a network of nodes connected by edges with non-negative weights. A constructive solution is given for finding the shortest path from a given node to all other nodes in the network.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.authors: Yao, S., Zhao, J., Yu, D., et al. (Princeton & Google)
papers.abstract: We explore using large language models to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner. ReAct prompts LLMs to generate verbal reasoning traces and actions for diverse language and decision making tasks, improving interpretability and performance.

papers.title: Generative AI for Adaptive Learning: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Chen, L., Patel, S., & Nguyen, T.
papers.abstract: This systematic review examines 87 studies on generative AI applications in adaptive learning systems. We analyze tutoring effectiveness, student engagement metrics, and ethical considerations for deploying LLM-based educational assistants in higher education.

papers.title: Gamification in Computer Science Education: A Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Rodriguez, M., Kim, H., & Okafor, E.
papers.abstract: We meta-analyze 42 controlled studies on gamification in CS education. Results show moderate positive effects on motivation and retention, with strongest gains in introductory programming courses when game mechanics align with learning objectives.

papers.title: IoT-Enabled Smart Grid Monitoring and Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Al-Ali, A. R., Zualkernan, I., Rashid, M., & Gupta, R.
papers.abstract: We propose an IoT-based architecture for real-time smart grid monitoring using edge sensors and cloud analytics. A hybrid CNN-LSTM model detects anomalies in power consumption patterns with 96.2% accuracy across three utility deployments.

papers.title: Optimal Integration of Renewable Energy Sources in Microgrids Using Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Hassan, F., Ahmed, S., & Khan, M. I.
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multi-agent coordination framework for integrating solar and wind generation in campus microgrids. Agents negotiate dispatch schedules to minimize cost while maintaining voltage stability under variable renewable output.

papers.title: Zero Trust Architecture
papers.authors: Rose, S., Borchert, O., Mitchell, S., & Connelly, D. (NIST)
papers.abstract: Zero trust is a cybersecurity paradigm focused on resource protection and the premise that trust is never granted implicitly. This document defines zero trust architecture components, deployment models, and use cases for enterprise and cloud environments.

papers.title: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples
papers.authors: Goodfellow, I., Shlens, J., & Szegedy, C.
papers.abstract: Several machine learning models, including neural networks, can be fooled by adversarial examples — inputs formed by applying small but intentionally worst-case perturbations. We explain these examples as a property of high-dimensional dot products and propose adversarial training as a defense.

papers.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption: A Survey of Applications in Secure Computing
papers.authors: Acar, A., Aksu, H., Uluagac, A. S., & Conti, M.
papers.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption enables computation on encrypted data without decryption. We survey FHE schemes, performance trade-offs, and emerging applications in privacy-preserving machine learning, secure cloud analytics, and encrypted database queries.

papers.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA-Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
papers.authors: Jinek, M., Chylinski, K., Fonfara, I., Hauer, M., Doudna, J. A., & Charpentier, E.
papers.abstract: We report a dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease, Cas9, that uses a guide RNA to direct sequence-specific cleavage of double-stranded DNA. This system provides a foundation for RNA-programmable genome editing across diverse organisms.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Genomics: A Concise Overview
papers.authors: Zou, J., Huss, M., Abbeel, A., Mohammadi, P., Torkamani, A., & Telenti, A.
papers.abstract: Deep learning is transforming genomics research by enabling accurate prediction of regulatory elements, variant effects, and protein structures from sequence data. We review architectures, datasets, and open challenges for applying neural networks to genomic problems.

papers.title: De Novo Protein Design by Deep Network Hallucination
papers.authors: Anishchenko, I., Pellock, S. J., Chidyausiku, T. M., et al. (UW & Meta)
papers.abstract: We describe a deep learning approach to generate novel protein backbones and sequences with desired functional properties. Network hallucination produces proteins that fold and function as predicted, expanding the toolkit for computational protein engineering.

papers.title: Quantum Supremacy Using a Programmable Superconducting Processor
papers.authors: Arute, F., Arya, K., Babbush, R., et al. (Google AI Quantum)
papers.abstract: We report the use of a processor with programmable superconducting qubits to create quantum states on 53 qubits. Sampling from the resulting state takes 200 seconds, while simulating the same task on a classical supercomputer would take approximately 10,000 years.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization and Discrete Logarithms on a Quantum Computer
papers.authors: Shor, P. W.
papers.abstract: We present efficient quantum algorithms for factoring integers and computing discrete logarithms. These algorithms threaten widely used public-key cryptosystems and motivate post-quantum cryptography research.

papers.title: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping: Part I
papers.authors: Thrun, S., Burgard, W., & Fox, D.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping is the computational problem of constructing a map of an unknown environment while simultaneously keeping track of the agent's location within it. This survey covers probabilistic approaches including EKF-SLAM and FastSLAM.

papers.title: Learning Complex Dexterous Manipulation with Deep Reinforcement Learning and Demonstrations
papers.authors: Rajeswaran, A., Kumar, V., Gupta, A., et al.
papers.abstract: We combine deep reinforcement learning with human demonstrations to solve complex dexterous manipulation tasks. Our approach leverages a small number of demonstrations to guide exploration, enabling a robotic hand to perform in-hand object reorientation.

papers.title: End-to-End Autonomous Driving: Challenges and Frontiers
papers.authors: Chen, L., Wu, P., Chisu, J., et al.
papers.abstract: We provide a comprehensive survey of end-to-end autonomous driving systems that map sensor inputs directly to control commands. We analyze perception, planning, safety verification, and sim-to-real transfer challenges for production deployment.

papers.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
papers.authors: Lundberg, S. M., & Lee, S. I.
papers.abstract: We present SHAP values as a unified measure of feature importance based on cooperative game theory. SHAP connects six existing explanation methods and provides consistent, locally accurate attributions for any machine learning model.

papers.title: Data Structures for Statistical Computing in Python
papers.authors: McKinney, W.
papers.abstract: We describe pandas, a Python library for data manipulation and analysis. pandas provides labeled data structures and operations for handling relational and time series data, becoming a foundational tool for statistical computing and data science workflows.

papers.title: A Density-Based Algorithm for Discovering Clusters in Large Spatial Databases with Noise
papers.authors: Ester, M., Kriegel, H. P., Sander, J., & Xu, X.
papers.abstract: We propose DBSCAN, a density-based clustering algorithm for discovering clusters of arbitrary shape in spatial databases with noise. DBSCAN requires only a minimum cluster size and a distance threshold, avoiding the need to specify the number of clusters.

papers.title: Feature Stores for Machine Learning: Principles, Practices, and Challenges
papers.authors: Hopsworks Team & Momentum Works
papers.abstract: Feature stores centralize the creation, storage, and serving of ML features across training and inference pipelines. We describe architectural patterns, consistency guarantees, and organizational practices for building production feature platforms.

papers.title: Mistral 7B
papers.authors: Jiang, A. Q., Sablayrolles, A., Mensch, A., et al. (Mistral AI)
papers.abstract: We introduce Mistral 7B, a 7-billion-parameter language model engineered for superior performance and efficiency. Mistral 7B outperforms Llama 2 13B on all benchmarks we tested, and approaches Llama 34B quality while enabling deployment on modest hardware.

papers.title: Segment Anything
papers.authors: Kirillov, A., Mintun, E., Ravi, N., et al. (Meta AI)
papers.abstract: We introduce the Segment Anything project: a new task, model, and dataset for image segmentation. Our promptable segmentation model SAM achieves strong zero-shot performance on diverse segmentation tasks and enables flexible interactive segmentation.

papers.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.authors: Touvron, H., Martin, L., Stone, K., et al. (Meta AI)
papers.abstract: We develop and release Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models ranging from 7B to 70B parameters. Llama 2-Chat models are optimized for dialogue use cases and demonstrate improvements in helpfulness and safety over Llama 1.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.authors: Dao, T., Fu, D., Ermon, S., Rudra, A., & Ré, C.
papers.abstract: We propose FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce memory reads/writes between GPU high bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM. FlashAttention trains Transformers faster and enables longer context lengths on the same hardware.

papers.title: Borg, Omega, and Kubernetes
papers.authors: Burns, B., Grant, B., Oppenheimer, D., Brewer, E., & Wilkes, J. (Google)
papers.abstract: We trace the evolution from Google's internal Borg cluster manager through Omega to Kubernetes, the open-source container orchestration system. We discuss design principles for large-scale cluster management and lessons learned from production deployments.
